summary: A 1941 ground cabin in Wyoming's Salt River Range, listed as standing, though a 2021 article describes only what remains.

facts.design: Ground cabin with four window panels per side; register gives dimensions as approximately 12x12
facts.status_note: A Wyoming lookout index lists it as standing; a 2021 KINGFM article describes only remains.

access.note: Reached on foot by a long hike; KINGFM reports nothing left that could be rented or used for accommodation.

visit.trail_note: About 20 miles round trip up Strawberry Creek to McDougal Pass, then on to the lookout (2021 hiking video, as quoted by KINGFM)

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Bridger-Teton National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1941 as the build year. A 2021 hiking video quoted by KINGFM dates it to the late 1930s or early 1940s and credits the Civilian Conservation Corps; builder not confirmed elsewhere.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 10,260 ft (3,127 m); firelookout.com gives 10,283 ft. The story uses the register figure and reports both.
The Wyoming index lists the cabin as standing; the 2021 KINGFM article describes only remains. The story reports both and does not claim a current site check.

sources.title: What's Left of an Abandoned Fire Lookout Tower in Wyoming

notes_for_editor: Build year 1941 rests on the register alone; the KINGFM CCC attribution is a hiking video's narration quoted second-hand and is unverified. The 'standing' status comes from the firelookout.org index, not the register text. The access level 'public' is inferred from the hiking account, not stated by any source. Brief record checked: name, county, elevation, agency and 2022 registration match the register, so no corrections. Not reached: Bridger-Teton lookout records or a Forest Service page on current status; a 2022 Wyoming fire report mentioning the Cabin Creek lookout cabin appeared in search but was not read. The story does not claim a current site check.
